items.title: Zero and out of range de rham cohomology
items.statement: $H^k=0$ for $k<0$ and $k>\dim M$.
items.strategy: The cochain group itself is zero outside 0,...,n; therefore its kernel and cohomology vanish there.

items.title: Zero th de rham cohomology is locally constant functions
items.statement: H^0_dR(M) is the algebra of locally constant real functions, canonically the product of R over the connected components. In particular H^0=R for connected nonempty M.
items.strategy: A closed zero-form has vanishing coordinate partial derivatives, hence is constant on coordinate balls. Its level sets are open and closed, so it is constant on each connected component. Components of a manifold are open, so arbitrary constants on them give smooth functions. Omega^-1=0 gives no quotient ambiguity; the empty manifold gives the zero vector space.

items.title: Pullback is a morphism of de rham complexes
items.statement: Every smooth F:M→N defines a cochain map F*:Omega^bullet(N)→Omega^bullet(M).
items.strategy: Pullback is degree-preserving and linear; the earlier identity dF*=F*d is exactly the cochain-map equation. Use zero maps in out-of-range degrees.

items.title: Pullback induces a well defined map on de rham cohomology

items.title: De rham cohomology is a contravariant functor
items.statement: Pullback on de Rham cohomology preserves identities and reverses composition.
items.strategy: Reindex cochains as Csharp_n=C^(-n), with unchanged differential. Apply homology functoriality to this reindexing and the pullback identities (G∘F)*=F*G* and id*=id.

items.title: Wedge with a closed form preserves exactness classes
items.statement: For closed alpha of degree p and beta of degree q, replacing alpha by alpha+d eta changes alpha wedge beta by d(eta wedge beta); replacing beta by beta+d theta changes it by d((-1)^p alpha wedge theta).
items.strategy: Apply the graded Leibniz rule with both closedness hypotheses. When both representatives change, perform the changes successively with the other still closed. This proves boundaries form an ideal in cycles, not merely that the product of two boundaries is a boundary.

items.title: Wedge product descends to de rham cohomology
items.statement: For closed forms alpha,beta, [alpha][beta]=[alpha wedge beta] defines a bilinear associative graded-commutative product on H^*_dR(M).
items.strategy: Leibniz proves closedness. Apply the preceding ideal lemma separately to each representative; inherit associativity, bilinearity and the sign (-1)^(pq) from wedge.

items.statement: Decompose a form on $M\times I$ uniquely as $\alpha_t+dt\wedge\beta_t$ locally and set $K\omega=\int_0^1\beta_t\,dt$; smoothness under the parameter integral is proved using `thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle`, iterated in local coordinates.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. Decompose a form on $M\times I$ uniquely as $\alpha_t+dt\wedge\beta_t$ locally and set $K\omega=\int_0^1\beta_t\,dt$; smoothness under the parameter integral is proved using `thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle`, iterated in local coordinates.

items.title: The interval homotopy operator is coordinate independent
items.statement: equivalently $K\omega=\int_0^1\iota_{\partial_t}\omega\,dt$ after restriction to each slice.
items.strategy: For each t use the canonical product splitting to contract with partial_t and pull back to the slice M×{t}. This is an intrinsic covector on M; integration of its evaluations is coordinate-independent by linearity. A local compact rectangle and repeated scalar differentiation under the integral show smoothness of every coefficient.

items.title: De rham homotopy formula on a product
items.strategy: Write omega=alpha_t+dt wedge beta_t. Then d omega=d_M alpha_t+dt wedge (partial_t alpha_t-d_M beta_t). Integrating gives Kd omega=alpha_1-alpha_0-d_M K omega by the fundamental theorem of calculus. This also covers degree zero with K=0 there and the zero out-of-range spaces.

items.strategy: Apply the product identity to F*omega; use dF*=F*d and i_t*F*=F_t*. The homotopy is smooth up to the interval boundary in the earlier extension convention.

items.statement: Smoothly homotopic smooth maps F0,F1:M→N induce equal maps H^k_dR(N)→H^k_dR(M) for all k.
items.strategy: For a closed omega, the two pullbacks differ by d(KF*omega), hence represent equal classes. Equivalently reindex the cochain homotopy and apply the earlier chain-homotopy theorem.

items.statement: Continuous homotopy equivalences between nonempty smooth manifolds induce inverse de Rham algebra isomorphisms after smooth approximation; continuously homotopic smooth maps induce equal maps.

items.title: Closed differential forms are locally exact
items.statement: Every closed smooth k-form with k≥1 admits a smooth primitive on a neighborhood of each point.
items.strategy: For a closed k-form with k≥1 restrict to a coordinate ball, transfer by the chart diffeomorphism, apply the star-shaped lemma and pull back its primitive. Degree zero is excluded.

items.title: De rham cohomology of a contractible smooth manifold
items.statement: $H^0\cong\mathbb R$ and $H^{k>0}=0$ for a nonempty connected contractible manifold.
items.strategy: A nonempty continuously contractible smooth manifold is continuously homotopy equivalent to a point. Use the preceding continuous invariance corollary (blocked until its smoothing interface is repaired), and compute the point complex directly.

items.title: Two open set de rham mayer vietoris cochain maps
items.statement: restriction $r:\Omega(M)\to\Omega(U)\oplus\Omega(V)$ and difference $s(\alpha,\beta)=\beta|_{U\cap V}-\alpha|_{U\cap V}$, with the sign fixed for the later connector.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. restriction $r:\Omega(M)\to\Omega(U)\oplus\Omega(V)$ and difference $s(\alpha,\beta)=\beta|_{U\cap V}-\alpha|_{U\cap V}$, with the sign fixed for the later connector.

items.title: The de rham mayer vietoris sequence is exact at the first two terms
items.statement: equal restrictions glue uniquely to a global smooth form.
items.strategy: Restriction is injective because equality of forms is local and U,V cover M. A pair lies in the difference-map kernel exactly when its restrictions agree; glue its smooth coordinate coefficients. Uniqueness is pointwise and d commutes with restriction.

items.title: The de rham mayer vietoris difference map is surjective
items.statement: For M=U union V and a smooth partition rho_U+rho_V=1 with support subordinate to U,V, every eta in Omega^k(U intersection V) has a difference-map preimage.
items.strategy: Define alpha=-rho_V eta on U intersection V and extend it by zero to U; define beta=rho_U eta and extend by zero to V. Support(rho_V) is closed in M and contained in V, so alpha is zero on a neighborhood of every point of U outside V. Likewise for beta. Then beta-alpha=eta. No compact support of eta is required.

items.title: Short exact mayer vietoris sequence of de rham complexes
items.statement: \[ 0\to\Omega^\bullet(M)\xrightarrow r \Omega^\bullet(U)\oplus\Omega^\bullet(V) \xrightarrow s\Omega^\bullet(U\cap V)\to0. \]
items.strategy: Assemble degreewise injectivity, kernel=image, and the partition-based surjectivity lemma. Both arrows commute with d by restriction naturality, including degrees with zero form spaces.

items.title: Mayer vietoris sequence in de rham cohomology
items.statement: cite HA's `thm-long-exact-sequence-in-cohomology`, including the direction $\delta:H^k(U\cap V)\to H^{k+1}(M)$.
items.strategy: Apply the published cohomology LES theorem to the established short exact sequence. Identify the cohomology of the middle finite direct sum with the direct sum of cohomologies by computing kernels and images componentwise. The connector increases degree: H^k(U∩V)→H^(k+1)(M).

items.title: Explicit de rham mayer vietoris connecting class
items.statement: With difference map s(alpha,beta)=beta-alpha, the connecting class of a closed eta on U intersection V is represented by the form whose restrictions are -d rho_V wedge eta on U and d rho_U wedge eta on V.
items.strategy: Differentiate the opposite-partition lifts. Their derivatives agree because d eta=0 and d rho_U=-d rho_V. Apply the published lift-differentiate-descend connector, reindexed cohomologically; its independence covers both lifts and representatives.

items.title: Naturality of de rham mayer vietoris for maps of covered manifolds
items.statement: A smooth map preserving the two named covering opens induces a contravariant morphism of the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequences, including the connecting maps.
items.strategy: For F:M→N with F(U)⊂Uprime and F(V)⊂Vprime, restrictions of F* commute with r and with s=second minus first. This gives a morphism from the N sequence to the M sequence. Invoke naturality of the cohomology connector to get F*delta_N=delta_M(F|_(U∩V))*; no cover-swapping sign is suppressed.

items.statement: finite only, avoiding an unexamined infinite product convention.
items.strategy: Restrict a form to each of finitely many open-and-closed components; conversely glue arbitrary component forms. These are inverse cochain maps, so kernels and images are finite direct sums. No infinite direct-sum assertion is made.

items.statement: for $n\ge2$, deform onto $S^{n-1}$; for $n=1$, treat the two contractible components separately; for $n=0$, the punctured space is empty and its de Rham cohomology is zero in every degree.

items.title: The de rham cohomology class of a form is defined without closedness
items.statement: Every smooth form defines a de Rham class.
items.strategy: On R^2, alpha=x dy has d alpha=dx wedge dy≠0; it is not in the numerator ker d.

items.title: Every smooth form is either closed or exact
items.statement: Every smooth form is either closed or exact.
items.strategy: The same x dy is not closed, and exact forms are closed by d^2=0.

items.title: Continuously homotopic smooth maps can be inserted directly into the differential form homotopy operator
items.statement: Every continuous homotopy between smooth maps can be inserted into the differential-form homotopy formula.
items.strategy: For maps point→R use H(t)=|t-1/2|: the endpoint maps are smooth but H is not differentiable at 1/2, so H*(dx) is not a smooth form. Apply the corrected relative smoothing theorem first.

items.title: The poincare lemma says every closed form is globally exact
items.statement: Every closed positive-degree form on every manifold is exact.
items.strategy: The angular form on punctured R^2 is closed and has period 2pi; the fundamental theorem for line integrals rules out exactness.

items.title: The mayer vietoris sequence is obtained by restricting forms without a partition of unity
items.statement: Restriction and unique gluing alone guarantee surjectivity of the two-open-set difference map.
items.strategy: Refute that inference with locally constant real functions on the two punctured-circle opens: both opens are connected but the overlap has two components; the difference map R^2 -> R^2 has diagonal image. For smooth forms surjectivity is true and is supplied by the partition construction; do not falsely claim that partitions are logically the only possible proof.

items.title: De rham cohomology is a covariant functor
items.statement: Smooth F:M→N canonically gives F*:H^*(M)→H^*(N).
items.strategy: Pullback takes forms on N to forms on M and reverses composition. The asserted type reverses its actual domain.

items.title: De rham cohomology of a point
items.statement: H^0_dR(point)=R and H^k=0 for k≠0.
items.strategy: All positive-degree alternating covectors on the zero tangent space vanish; d on constants is zero.

items.title: De rham cohomology of euclidean space
items.statement: For n≥0, H^0_dR(R^n)=R and H^k=0 for k>0.
items.strategy: Contract to zero by F(x,t)=tx and apply the homotopy formula.

items.title: De rham cohomology of a finite discrete manifold
items.statement: For a finite discrete zero-manifold of m points, H^0=R^m with coordinatewise product and H^k=0 for k≠0, including m=0.
items.strategy: Restrict forms to points and use the finite-disjoint-union result.

items.title: De rham cohomology of the circle from mayer vietoris
items.statement: H^0_dR(S^1)=H^1_dR(S^1)=R; other groups vanish.
items.strategy: Remove two distinct points to form contractible opens U,V; U∩V has two contractible components. The degree-zero difference map sends (a,b) to (b-a,b-a), with one-dimensional kernel and cokernel. Apply exactness.

items.title: The angular form generates the first de rham cohomology of the circle
items.statement: The restriction of (x dy-y dx)/(2pi) to the unit circle has period one and generates H^1_dR(S^1).
items.strategy: Parametrize by (cos t,sin t), integrate dt/(2pi) from 0 to 2pi. Exact forms have zero period by Stokes; the preceding dimension computation finishes.

items.title: De rham cohomology of the two sphere
items.strategy: Use the sphere theorem with n=2, displaying the connecting isomorphism from H^1 of the equatorial cylinder.

items.title: The standard volume form generates top cohomology of a sphere
items.statement: For n≥1 the standard outward-oriented sphere n-form generates H^n_dR(S^n).
items.strategy: The form is the restriction of contraction of Euclidean (n+1)-volume by the radial vector. It is a positive top form and has strictly positive integral by a positive chart bump and compactness; if exact Stokes would give zero. Combine with the sphere theorem.

items.title: De rham cohomology of punctured three space
items.statement: Punctured R^3 has H^0=H^2=R and all other groups zero.
items.strategy: The radial homotopy ((1-t)+t/|x|)x retracts onto S^2 without reaching zero.

items.title: Homotopy equivalent annulus and circle have isomorphic de rham rings
items.statement: For 0<a<b, the annulus a<|x|<b has the circle cohomology ring: R in degrees zero and one, with the square of its degree-one generator zero.
items.strategy: Choose r0 in (a,b); interpolate radii to r0, staying within (a,b). Radial projection and inclusion give inverse smooth homotopy equivalences. No Kunneth theorem is used.

items.title: The closed angular form on the punctured plane is not exact
items.statement: The form (x dy-y dx)/(x^2+y^2) on punctured R^2 is closed but not exact.
items.strategy: Differentiate the coordinate expression to get zero. Its integral around the unit circle is 2pi, whereas a global differential has zero period.

references.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, Lectures on the Geometry of Manifolds (author-hosted 702-page PDF)

items.title: The pullback on cohomology reverses composition order
items.statement: For F:M→N and G:N→P the induced map is (G∘F)*=F*∘G*, with domain H^*(P).
items.strategy: Display domains and codomains. A purported G*∘F* generally is not composable; the correct identity follows on representatives.

items.title: An explicit mayer vietoris connecting form on the circle
items.statement: A nonconstant locally constant class on the two components of U∩V for the punctured-circle cover has a nonzero Mayer–Vietoris connecting class.
items.strategy: Choose eta=0 on one component and 1 on the other; it is not in the diagonal image (b-a,b-a). Its connector has U-representative -d rho_V eta and V-representative d rho_U eta, extended by zero with the support argument. Exactness proves nonzero; normalize its period with the chosen orientation if desired.

items.title: Coordinate criterion for a riemannian metric
items.statement: the matrix $(g_{ij})$ is smooth, symmetric, and positive definite, and transforms tensorially.
items.strategy: The tensor-component criterion proves smoothness equivalence. Symmetry and positivity are invariant under congruence G_new=J^T G_old J with invertible transition Jacobian J; local matrices satisfying this law glue uniquely.

items.title: Every smooth manifold admits a riemannian metric
items.statement: Assuming AC_omega, every Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold admits a smooth Riemannian metric.
items.strategy: Under AC_omega apply the published tangent-bundle metric corollary of smooth bundle-metric existence. Its positive symmetric section is a smooth (0,2)-tensor by the tensor-bundle identification. No stronger existence axiom is asserted.

items.title: Pullback riemannian metric
items.statement: $(F^*h)_p(v,w)=h_{F(p)}(dF_pv,dF_pw)$.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. $(F^*h)_p(v,w)=h_{F(p)}(dF_pv,dF_pw)$.

items.title: Pullback of a riemannian metric is riemannian exactly for immersions
items.statement: without injectivity of $dF$ it is merely positive semidefinite.
items.strategy: For each tangent vector v, (F*h)(v,v)=h(dFv,dFv), which is positive exactly when dFv≠0. Thus positivity on every nonzero vector is equivalent to injectivity of dF at every point. Tensor pullback supplies smoothness and symmetry.

items.statement: An isometry is a diffeomorphism F with F*h=g. A local isometry is a smooth map between manifolds of the same dimension with F*h=g. An isometric immersion may have larger target dimension.
items.strategy: The dimension restriction is essential for the inverse function theorem in the next item.

items.strategy: Use pullback composition and inverse identities; pointwise injectivity and equal dimension make dF invertible, then apply the manifold inverse function theorem.

items.title: The gradient is characterized by inner products
items.statement: $g(\operatorname{grad}f,X)=Xf$.
items.strategy: The equality flat(grad f)=df gives g(grad f,X)=df(X)=Xf. Conversely a vector field with this pairing has the same flat image, hence equals grad f by injectivity.

items.title: Riemannian metrics induce metrics on dual tensor and exterior bundles
items.statement: define them on decomposable tensors and extend, proving independence through the universal property/basis formula.
items.strategy: Transport g to the dual with sharp; define tensor-product pairing multiplicatively. On decomposable exterior covectors set their pairing to det(<alpha_i,beta_j>). Alternation and multilinearity give a well-defined form, with ordered wedge monomials of an orthonormal coframe orthonormal. This determinant normalization avoids the k! discrepancy from an unnormalized antisymmetrization. The matrix formulas prove smoothness.

items.title: Riemannian speed and length
items.statement: $L_g(\gamma)=\int_a^b|\dot\gamma(t)|_gdt$.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. $L_g(\gamma)=\int_a^b|\dot\gamma(t)|_gdt$.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (C3.3b, 2014)

items.title: Riemannian length is independent of piecewise smooth subdivision
items.statement: The sum of the speed integrals over a finite C1 subdivision of a continuous piecewise C1 curve is independent of that subdivision.
items.strategy: Refine any two finite subdivisions by their union. On each common smooth piece the speed is the same; finite additivity of Riemann integrals gives equal sums. One-sided derivative values at finitely many breakpoints do not change the integral.

items.title: Riemannian length is invariant under orientation preserving piecewise c one reparametrization
items.statement: If gamma is continuous piecewise C1 and phi is a nondecreasing onto piecewise C1 reparametrization of compact intervals, L_g(gamma∘phi)=L_g(gamma), including flat intervals.
items.strategy: For a nondecreasing onto piecewise C1 map phi:[c,d]→[a,b], the chain rule gives speed(gamma∘phi)=speed(gamma)(phi) phi prime where defined. Refine at breakpoints and apply monotone Riemann substitution to the bounded piecewise continuous speed. Flat intervals contribute zero; constant pieces at a corner remain constant. A strictly increasing diffeomorphism is the standard special case.

items.title: Length is additive under concatenation and invariant under reversal
items.statement: Concatenated curves have the sum of the two lengths, and reversing a curve leaves its length unchanged.
items.strategy: Concatenate after affine rescaling to adjacent intervals and use subdivision independence and integral additivity. Reversal has derivative minus the original velocity, whose norm is unchanged; the decreasing substitution has absolute Jacobian.

items.title: Local comparison of a riemannian metric with the euclidean metric
items.statement: If (W,x) is a chart and K is a compact subset of W, there are positive constants c,C such that c|v|^2 <= g_ij(x(p))v^i v^j <= C|v|^2 for every p in K. Dimension zero is vacuous.
items.strategy: For positive dimension take the minimum and maximum of the continuous positive function (p,v) -> g_p(v,v) on K times the Euclidean unit sphere. K must be compact inside the chart domain: relatively compact in M alone does not control a chart at its artificial edge. If K is empty choose c=C=1. Otherwise the compact Euclidean coordinate image of K times S^(n-1) is nonempty and compact by Heine–Borel; its strictly positive minimum supplies c.

items.title: Any two points in a connected smooth manifold can be joined by a piecewise smooth curve
items.statement: connected plus local path connectedness gives path connectedness, then finitely many chart segments smooth the path.
items.strategy: Fix p and let E be the set reachable by finitely many smooth chart segments. Each point has a convex coordinate ball (half-ball if needed). Every such ball meeting E lies in E; the same observation makes its complement open. E is nonempty and clopen, so connectedness gives E=M. This avoids selecting an infinite family of paths.

items.title: Riemannian distance on a connected manifold
items.statement: On a connected Riemannian manifold define d_g(p,q)=inf L_g(gamma), over continuous piecewise C1 curves on compact intervals joining p to q. Smooth chart polygonal curves prove that this family is nonempty.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. $d_g(p,q)=\inf L_g(\gamma)$ over piecewise smooth curves from $p$ to $q$.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (C3.3b, 2014)
Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)

items.title: Riemannian distance is a metric
items.statement: On every connected Riemannian manifold d_g is finite, symmetric, separates points, and satisfies the triangle inequality.
items.strategy: Use piecewise smooth reachability for finiteness; reversal and epsilon-minimizing concatenation for symmetry and triangle inequality. First exit from a compact coordinate ball about p supplies a positive lower length bound for any curve to q outside that ball. Handle p=q with the constant curve.

references.title: Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)

items.title: The riemannian distance topology is the manifold topology
items.statement: On a connected Riemannian manifold the metric d_g induces exactly the manifold topology.
items.strategy: Choose nested coordinate balls with compact larger closure inside one chart. A path that exits the larger ball has a uniformly positive length before first exit; paths staying inside satisfy the Euclidean lower bound. Straight coordinate segments give the upper bound. Derive both neighborhood inclusions without geodesics or Hopf-Rinow.

references.title: Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)

items.title: Length dominates endpoint distance
items.statement: For every piecewise C1 curve gamma:[a,b]→M, d_g(gamma(a),gamma(b))≤L_g(gamma).
items.strategy: Every piecewise C1 curve joining p and q is one of the competitors in the defining infimum, hence d_g(p,q)≤L_g(gamma).

items.title: A smooth map with pointwise operator norm at most c is c lipschitz for riemannian distance
items.statement: For connected Riemannian M,N, c≥0, and smooth F:M→N satisfying |dF_p v|_h≤c|v|_g everywhere, d_h(Fp,Fq)≤c d_g(p,q).
items.strategy: Assume c≥0 and connected source and target, and |dF_p v|_h≤c|v|_g for every p,v. The chain rule bounds the image speed, integration bounds image length, and taking the infimum over source curves gives d_h(Fp,Fq)≤c d_g(p,q). No injectivity of F is needed.

items.title: Riemannian isometries preserve length and distance
items.statement: Every Riemannian isometry preserves curve lengths and the induced distance on each component.
items.strategy: The metric identity gives equality of curve speeds. Apply the c=1 inequality to F and its inverse to get both distance inequalities.

items.title: Extended riemannian distance on a disconnected manifold
items.statement: distance between components is $+\infty$, so no finite metric is falsely claimed globally.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. distance between components is $+\infty$, so no finite metric is falsely claimed globally.

items.title: Distance from a point to a subset
items.statement: Define d_g(p,A)=inf_{a∈A}d_g(p,a), with infimum of the empty family +infinity.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. Specialize the named A-page results; give the concrete object and verify the hypotheses.

items.title: Distance to a nonempty subset is one lipschitz
items.statement: on a connected Riemannian manifold it is finite-valued and $1$-Lipschitz. More generally, on a component $C$ with $A\cap C\ne\varnothing$, the restriction $x\mapsto d(x,A\cap C)$ is finite-valued and $1$-Lipschitz. No finite-valued assertion is made on a component disjoint from $A$ under the extended-distance convention.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. on a connected Riemannian manifold it is finite-valued and $1$-Lipschitz. More generally, on a component $C$ with $A\cap C\ne\varnothing$, the restriction $x\mapsto d(x,A\cap C)$ is finite-valued and $1$-Lipschitz. No finite-valued assertion is made on a component disjoint from $A$ under the extended-distance convention.

items.title: Riemannian volume density
items.statement: In every coordinate chart the metric density is sqrt(det(g_ij)) |dx^1 ... dx^n|.
items.strategy: Use the positive square root; the following lemma checks compatibility.

references.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, Lectures on the Geometry of Manifolds (author-hosted 702-page PDF)
references.locator: p.66; Definition 2.2.72 densities; Example 2.2.73 metric density

items.title: The riemannian volume density is coordinate independent
items.statement: the metric determinant transforms by the square of the inverse Jacobian, leaving the density's absolute-Jacobian law.
items.strategy: Under x=x(y), the new metric matrix is J^T G J. Its positive determinant square root is |det J|sqrt(det G), exactly the transition law for density coefficients, so the local expressions glue.

items.title: Riemannian volume form on an oriented manifold
items.statement: $dV_g=\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ in every positively oriented chart.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. $dV_g=\sqrt{\det(g_{ij})}\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ in every positively oriented chart.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (C3.3b, 2014)
Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)
references.locator: pp.57–58; 9.4 Orientability and Riemannian volume form: main construction

items.title: The riemannian volume form is the unique positive unit top form
items.statement: On an oriented Riemannian n-manifold, the metric volume form is the unique positive smooth top form of pointwise norm one.
items.strategy: In a positively oriented orthonormal coframe, the wedge of all basis covectors is the only positive top covector of unit norm. Under oriented orthonormal frame changes its determinant is +1. In coordinates this is sqrt(det G) dx^1 wedge ... wedge dx^n.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (C3.3b, 2014)
references.locator: p.79; Proposition 9.1 existence of volume form

items.title: Riemannian volume of a compactly supported smooth density
items.statement: For a compactly supported smooth function f, define its metric integral as the already constructed integral of the smooth density f dV_g. For compact M this defines total volume by f=1.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. cite DG-14.

items.title: Riemannian volume measure
items.statement: The intended extension is a locally finite Radon Borel measure vol_g with chart formula vol_g(A)=integral_(x(A)) sqrt(det(g_ij)) dx for Borel A contained in a chart, and its completion for measurable sets. It assigns volume to arbitrary metric balls. This claim is BLOCKED pending the prerequisite pair specified in the batch notes.
items.strategy: Do not infer a measurable-set construction from compactly supported smooth Riemann integration. Prove chartwise compatibility by Lebesgue change of variables, glue a countable atlas, establish independence, local finiteness and regularity, then agreement with the earlier smooth integral. The current plan does not supply this interface; preserve the claim as an open obligation.

items.title: Riemannian divergence
items.statement: $\mathcal L_XdV_g=(\operatorname{div}_gX)dV_g$; this is orientation independent because the density version agrees.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. $\mathcal L_XdV_g=(\operatorname{div}_gX)dV_g$; this is orientation independent because the density version agrees.

items.title: Coordinate formula for riemannian divergence
items.statement: $\operatorname{div}_gX=|g|^{-1/2}\partial_i(|g|^{1/2}X^i)$.
items.strategy: Apply the earlier volume-form divergence formula to the positive local coefficient sqrt(det G). On reversing orientation both the form and its Lie derivative change sign, leaving the quotient unchanged; this glues the same function for the density convention.

items.title: Riemannian divergence theorem
items.statement: For an oriented smooth Riemannian n-manifold with boundary, n≥1, and compactly supported smooth vector field X, integral_M div_g(X)dV_g = integral_boundaryM g(X,nu)dV_boundaryg, with outward unit normal nu and outward-first induced orientation.
items.strategy: For n>=1 and compactly supported X on an oriented Riemannian manifold with boundary, form the outward unit normal from minus the musical gradient of a boundary-defining function divided by its positive norm, and glue by uniqueness. In a positively oriented orthonormal boundary frame prove j^*(i_X dV_g)=g(X,nu)dV_boundary. Apply the published volume-form divergence theorem. Metric existence on boundary charts uses the earlier boundary partition theorem. Include this normal construction explicitly, without Levi-Civita.

items.title: Riemannian hodge star
items.statement: the unique map $*: \bigwedge^kT^*M\to\bigwedge^{n-k}T^*M$ satisfying $\alpha\wedge *\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_gdV_g$ on an oriented Riemannian manifold.
items.strategy: Use precisely the declared prerequisites. the unique map $*: \bigwedge^kT^*M\to\bigwedge^{n-k}T^*M$ satisfying $\alpha\wedge *\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_gdV_g$ on an oriented Riemannian manifold. For the constant rescaling gprime=t^2 g, t>0, the k-covector pairing scales by t^(-2k), volume by t^n, and hence starprime=t^(n-2k)star by its defining identity.

items.title: Hodge star is a smooth bundle isomorphism
items.statement: construct it in an oriented orthonormal coframe.
items.strategy: On an oriented orthonormal coframe send the wedge indexed by I to the complementary wedge with the permutation sign for (I,Icomplement). This is the unique map satisfying the defining pairing, hence is independent of the coframe. Smooth local orthonormal coframes follow by finite Gram–Schmidt with positive smooth denominators; the explicit invertible matrix proves smoothness.

items.title: Hodge star squared sign
items.statement: $*^2=(-1)^{k(n-k)}$ on $k$-forms in the positive-definite convention.
items.strategy: Apply the complementary-index basis formula twice. Interchanging blocks of k and n-k covectors requires k(n-k) transpositions, giving (-1)^(k(n-k)); degree zero and n follow from the same calculation.

references.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, Lectures on the Geometry of Manifolds (author-hosted 702-page PDF)

items.title: Riemannian inner product of compactly supported forms
items.statement: $(\alpha,\beta)=\int_M\alpha\wedge *\beta$ is positive definite.
items.strategy: The pointwise identity alpha wedge *beta=<alpha,beta>dV gives symmetry and bilinearity. If alpha is nonzero, |alpha|^2 is positive on some chart neighborhood; multiply by a nonzero supported bump there to obtain a strictly positive integral lower bound. Compact support ensures every integral exists. Thus zero norm forces alpha=0.

items.title: The codifferential and hodge theory
items.statement: The sign convention suggests delta on k-forms as (-1)^(n(k+1)+1) * d *; adjoint identities, elliptic estimates, harmonic representatives and Hodge decomposition require a later analytic treatment.
items.strategy: Record only the formal operator convention; no analytic Hodge theorem, adjoint-domain result or decomposition is used by this batch.

items.title: The pullback of a riemannian metric by every smooth map is a riemannian metric
items.statement: Every smooth map pulls a Riemannian metric back to a Riemannian metric.
items.strategy: A constant map R→R has zero differential and pulls dx^2 back to zero.

items.title: Every riemannian manifold has finite distance between points in different components
items.statement: Riemannian distance between points of distinct components is finite.
items.strategy: Two disjoint Euclidean lines have no cross-component path; infimum of the empty family is +infinity.

items.title: Riemannian distance is defined by the length of a unique shortest curve
items.statement: Every pair of points is joined by a unique shortest curve whose length defines distance.
items.strategy: On punctured R^2 with Euclidean metric, (-1,0) and (1,0) have infimum length 2, approached by detours around zero, but equality in the Euclidean endpoint bound would force a straight segment through zero. On the unit circle antipodes have two minimizing semicircles; prove the lower bound inline by finite angular-chart lifting.

items.title: The riemannian volume form exists on every riemannian manifold
items.statement: Every Riemannian manifold carries a positive global Riemannian volume form.
items.strategy: A nowhere-zero top form determines an orientation. A nonorientable manifold, for instance the Mobius band, admits a metric by metric existence but cannot carry such a form. The metric density still exists.

items.title: The distance function is smooth on all of m times m
items.statement: Riemannian distance is smooth on all of M×M.
items.strategy: Already on the Euclidean line d(x,y)=|x-y| is not differentiable on x=y. The circle also fails smoothness at antipodal pairs; derive from the two angular arc lengths inline.

items.title: The hodge star is defined without an orientation
items.statement: The ordinary top-form-valued Hodge star is determined by the metric alone.
items.strategy: Reverse the orientation of an oriented Euclidean space. Volume changes sign and the defining wedge identity forces star to change sign, with the metric unchanged.

title: Riemannian Metrics Length Distance and Volume — Examples

items.title: The euclidean metric and its musical maps
items.statement: For g=sum dx_i^2 on R^n, flat and sharp preserve coordinate coefficients and grad f=sum partial_i f partial_i.
items.strategy: Insert the identity matrix in the musical and gradient formulas.

references.title: Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)

items.title: The round metric on the sphere as an induced metric
items.statement: The round sphere metric is the pullback of the Euclidean metric under S^n→R^(n+1); on S^2 away from the poles it is dtheta^2+sin^2(theta)dphi^2.
items.strategy: The inclusion has injective differential. Differentiate the spherical parametrization and compute its Gram matrix; do not extend the singular chart through the poles.

references.title: Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)

items.title: The product riemannian metric
items.statement: On M×N the direct sum g⊕h is a smooth positive metric with block diagonal matrix; a Euclidean line times a circle gives the flat cylinder.
items.strategy: Split tangent vectors into the two factors, add their squared norms, and compute the block determinant for volume.

items.title: A conformal metric on the plane
items.statement: For smooth u on R^2, e^(2u)(dx^2+dy^2) has speed e^u|v|, volume density e^(2u)|dx dy| and grad_g f=e^(-2u)grad_E f.
items.strategy: Calculate the inverse matrix and determinant. For the ball model 4(1-|x|^2)^(-2)g_E on |x|<1, radial length from zero to radius r is log((1+r)/(1-r)); this is a length calculation, not a completeness theorem.

references.title: Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)
references.locator: pp.47–48; Example 8.2.5 Poincare ball radial length

items.title: The hyperbolic upper half space metric
items.statement: On x_n>0 the upper-half-space metric is x_n^(-2)sum dx_i^2, with density x_n^(-n)|dx|; a vertical segment between heights a,b has length |log(b/a)|.
items.strategy: Positive height ensures smooth positivity. Substitute a vertical curve in the length integral; no curvature or completeness assertion is inferred.

references.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (C3.3b, 2014)
Ved V. Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry (September 11, 2025)

items.title: The flat torus metric from periodic euclidean coordinates
items.statement: The product (S^1)^n with unit circle metrics has Euclidean metric matrices in local angle coordinates and total smooth volume (2pi)^n.
items.strategy: On overlapping angle charts, transitions are translations by multiples of 2pi, so the local matrices glue. Use a finite product chart partition for the integral; this constructs the periodic metric without assuming a covering-space theorem.

items.title: Length and distance on the circle
items.statement: On the unit circle, the distance between angles theta and phi is min_(m∈Z)|theta-phi+2pi m|, and antipodal points have two shortest semicircles.
items.strategy: Subdivide any curve into angular charts and continue its angle across finitely many pieces. Its lifted endpoint differs by 2pi m; integral |theta prime| bounds the endpoint difference. The shorter arc attains the minimum.

items.title: A riemannian distance with no cross component finite value
items.statement: On the disjoint union of two Euclidean lines there is no curve joining different components; extended distance there is +infinity.
items.strategy: The image of the connected parameter interval is connected. Within each component distance is the usual absolute difference.

items.title: Volume density in polar coordinates
items.statement: On the punctured plane in a polar chart, g=dr^2+r^2 dtheta^2 and dV=r|dr dtheta| for r>0.
items.strategy: Compute the Jacobian Gram matrix and positive square root of its determinant. The polar chart excludes the origin and an angular cut.

items.title: Hodge star on euclidean three space
items.statement: With dx wedge dy wedge dz positive in R^3, *dx=dy wedge dz, *dy=dz wedge dx, *dz=dx wedge dy, *1=dx wedge dy wedge dz, and *^2=1.
items.strategy: Verify the defining wedge pairing on the orthonormal basis and complement signs.

references.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, Lectures on the Geometry of Manifolds (author-hosted 702-page PDF)

items.title: Divergence in polar coordinates
items.statement: For X=X^r partial_r+X^theta partial_theta on a polar chart, div X=r^(-1)partial_r(rX^r)+partial_theta X^theta.
items.strategy: Use sqrt(det g)=r in the coordinate divergence formula. X^theta is the coordinate coefficient, not the orthonormal angular component; replacing it by X_hat_theta/r gives the usual physical-component formula.

items.title: A degenerate pullback metric under a constant map
items.statement: A constant map from a positive-dimensional manifold pulls any target metric back to the zero bilinear form, which is not positive definite.
items.strategy: Its differential vanishes; any nonzero tangent vector has zero pulled-back squared norm.
